The following are brief descriptions of the major unit processes, operations, and/or equipment: a. Return activated sludge and waste activated sludge is pumped by airlift pump. c. Tertiary Treatment: Tertiary treatment is provided through coagulation, rapid mix, flocculation, and sand filtration. Solids Handling: The waste activated sludge is aerobically digested and pumped to a centrifuge for partial thickening. The thickened, digested sludge is stored in a 10,000-gallon underground storage tank prior to hauling to the Donald C. chunks.text: The primary stage of wastewater treatment is the removal of both grit and primary sludge. Grit is represented in the model as solid-state silicon dioxide which is about 1% of the total inlet water flow. The grit in wastewater has a specific gravity in the range 1.5-2.7 kg/l which is much higher than that of the organic matter suspended in the influent stream (1.02 kg/l). A differential sedimentation can thus be a successful mechanism for separating grit from organic matter (Liu and Lipták, 2000) . A density-based classifier is defined as a unit operation to remove the grit in this model. The primary treatment can reduce the Total Suspended Solids (TSS) by 50-60%. Also, it implies the removal of the BOD in the incoming wastewater by 20-30%. The percentage of the sludge removal chosen in the present model is 55%.

It has a total height of 4 m, and occupies a surface area of 1500 m 2 and a volume of 6000 m 3 . A fraction of the sludge flows out of the system in the form of waste at a flow rate of 385 m 3 /d, corresponding to a biomass age of 9 days, while the other fraction is recycled externally to the first tank at a rate of 18,446 m 3 /d. The biological processes occurring in both biological reactors are simulated using the IWA Activated Sludge Model No. 1 (ASM1) proposed by [47] . This model uses thirteen state variables to track the fate of biodegradable, non-biodegradable, soluble, insoluble, nitrogen, and carbon materials. These state variables are linked to eight degradation bioprocesses occurring in biological reactors.

chunks.text: A pilot-scale system, consisting of a grit tank and microscreen for primary treatment followed by a SAF-MBR 2.0 for secondary treatment, was installed at the Codiga Resource Recovery Center (Stanford, CA), as illustrated in. The pilot-scale system treated municipal wastewater pumped from the Serra Street sewer on the Stanford campus for more than three years. Sewage was de-gritted in a grit tank then subject to primary treatment by screening through a 0.3 mm pore size microscreen (MS-28, Hydro International). The pilot-scale SAF-MBR 2.0 consisted of: (1) two AFBRs operated in parallel, hereafter referred to as AFBR 1 and AFBR 2, containing fluidized GAC biocarrier, and (2) a gas-sparged membrane tank equipped with ultrafiltration membranes. Recirculation of bulk fluid (twice the influent flow rate) between the three reactors enabled complete mixing and control of solids accumulation within the gas-sparged membrane tank.

chunks.text: Water is one of the most important resources for human survival. The water demand has pronounced over the past decades due to population growth, industry development, and agricultural expansion. Although groundwater, surface water, and rainwater are conventional freshwater resources, nowadays, unconventional water resources such as wastewater are recognized as valuable resources for freshwater supply. In this regard, wastewater treatment and reuse have become viable selections for providing additional water supplies (Kim and Jang, 2006) . Membrane bioreactor (MBR) systems are one of the most promising wastewater treatment technologies growing increasingly all over the world, especially in developing countries (Wu et al., 2008) . Membrane bioreactors combine conventional activated sludge (CAS) and membrane separation technologies to produce high-quality water (Zhang et al., 2021) . MBR technology reduces plant footprint by eliminating clarifiers and conventional filters, which makes them more efficient in comparison with conventional wastewater treatment processes (Judd, 2010; Deng et al., 2015) .

chunks.text: This study deals with wastewater treatment on a pilot-scale plant set up by electrochemical technology. The electrocoagulation and electroflocculation techniques were applied with a revived design to meet the needs of the process to remove suspended solids and micropollutants out of the wastewater stream. By using various settings of applied currents, the process was tested for the better quality of effluent using water from the outflow of primary sedimentation tank and treated water from the outflow of secondary sedimentation tank. Furthermore, the results are optimized for a better downstream separation process. Wastewater from primary sedimentation tank was treated with both Fe and Al electrodes. In the case of Fe electrodes, more than 50 % of COD removal was observed which was about 12-18 % with Al electrodes. The coagulation dose of Fe and Al electrodes were measured, on the basis of AFS produced and according to Faraday's Law. With both Fe and Al electrodes, the coagulation dose went on increasing with increasing current density.

chunks.text: In recent years, problems with access to clean and safe water as well as the global water crisis and strict legal regulations in waste management have forced municipal facilities to reconsider and implement third-and fourth-degree wastewater treatment. Examples of interest in secondary wastewater treatment processes include municipal facilities worldwide, e.g. the Waldwick wastewater treatment plant (New Jersey, USA) [12] or the Point Loma wastewater treatment plant (San Diego, USA) [13] . The Waldwick WWTP conducts secondary wastewater treatment using processes involving ultraviolet lamps to achieve the ultimate wastewater disinfection without the necessity of applying chlorine. By 2025, the Point Loma WWTP plans to produce about 129 000 m 3 /d of potable water from municipal waste by utilizing biological processes (biological activated carbon), membrane processes (microfiltration, reverse osmosis) and advanced oxidation (UV radiation, ozone, hydrogen peroxide). The application of secondary treatment processes depends on a WWTP's location (e.g. recreational areas, housing infrastructure, industrial areas, protected land, agricultural areas), therefore the end goals of secondary treatment may include e.g. agricultural irrigation, street and square cleaning, process water production for equipment cleaning, aquifer recharging by injection wells.

chunks.text: Preliminary treatment is the initial stage where coarse particles and foreign matter commonly found in raw wastewater are removed to optimize subsequent treatment processes (Sonune and Ghate, 2004) . This stage involves activities such as coarse screening, grit removal, and the comminution of large objects in wastewater. Grit chambers maintain high water velocities, preventing organic compounds from settling within the chamber. Although not all wastewater treatment plants incorporate grit removal in their preliminary treatment, some employ comminutors alongside coarse screening to reduce the size of large particles. Additionally, flow measurement devices and wave flumes are commonly used during this phase (Pachwarya et al., 2021) . It's crucial to remove oil and grease from wastewater at this stage to mitigate its adverse effects on the subsequent treatment processes. This is typically achieved through methods such as chlorination, vacuum flotation, and aeration (Pachwarya et al., 2021) .

chunks.text: In the activated sludge process the majority of biological solids removed in the secondary sedimentation tank are recycled (returned sludge). The feedback of most of the cell yields from the sedimentation tank encourages rapid adsorption of the pollutants in the incoming settled sewage and also serves to stabilize the operation over a wide range of dilution rates and substrate concentrations imposed by fluctuations in the flow and strength of the wastewater. Secondary treatment processes can remove up to 95 per cent of the BOD and suspended solids entering the process, as well as significant amounts of heavy metals and certain organic compounds which could otherwise cause the deterioration of chemical and ecological quality of receiving waters [10, 53] . Conventional wastewater treatment usually ends with secondary treatment which cannot efficiently remove all the different compounds found in sewage and therefore treated effluents are one of the main sources of persistent micropollutants in the environment [1, 62] . For water reuse, tertiary treatment is needed to provide additional removal of contaminants such as microbial pathogens, particulates, or nutrients, and advanced treatment processes are employed when wastewater is to be reclaimed for reuse, depending on the type of use and quality requirements [49] .

chunks.text: Based on a survey on pre-treatment measures for 17 full-scale AeMBRs, the following information deserves special attention (Itokawa et al., 2008) : 1) grit chamber, coarse and fine screenings are mostly essential for MBR operation to removal grits, large suspended particles and long fibers, with fine screening (3 mm for FS membrane and 0.5-1 mm for HF membrane) installed universally; and 2) using the "by pass sieving" method, which recycles part of the suspended sludge through a sieve, achieves the further removal of unfavorable substances accumulated in the bioreactor. These means can be extended to AnMBRs minimizing the presence of undesirable substances into the bioreactor while with adequate consideration of keeping strict anaerobic environment. A recent novel concept, referred to as wastewater pre-concentration (Ansari et al., 2016) , is still under investigation, but has shown great potential to enhance bioresource recovery and energy generation efficiency (Guven et al., 2019) , accompanied by a low volumetric flow rate and process footprint (Alvarado et al., 2020) .

chunks.text: The GAC pilot study was conducted at the municipal wastewater treatment plant Muenchehofe (Berlin, Germany) over a consecutive period of ten months. The WWTP treats up to 42,500 m 3 /d by primary sedimentation, biological activated sludge treatment with chemical precipitation and secondary clarification. Characteristics of the secondary effluent during the experimental period are given in Table 1 . The pilot plant consists of two identical filter columns, each with a diameter of 0.15 m and a height of 4 m. One filter is operated as dual-media downflow filter, whereas the other filter uses only GAC as filter material and is fed in upflow direction. GAC Epibon A 8 Â 30 mesh was supplied by Donau Carbon, Germany. Upon filling the filter columns, the GAC was wetted for two days and backwashed several times to remove undersized particles. The dual-media filter uses 1.4 m GAC and 0.6 m quartz sand (0.7e1.1 mm) as filter material.
